articles.title: Losing Award, Keeping Shield: Section 9 Limits
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has issued a new ruling under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, addressing the limits of interim legal protection for parties challenging arbitration awards. The decision explores how courts can balance granting protection to losing parties without undermining the finality of arbitration awards. This ruling impacts India's arbitration laws and enforcement mechanisms, as Section 34 and Section 36 of the Act govern challenges to awards and their enforcement
articles.raw_summary: After Home Care Retail Marts [1] , the Supreme Court's latest Section 9 decision poses a tougher question: once the losing party is allowed legal protection, how far may the court go without turning interim protection into an appeal against the award? articles.title: Behind the Label Lies a Longer and Stranger Chemical Story

This raises concerns about pollution and sustainability in the textile industry, which is a major sector in India.

articles.title: Google agrees to settle UK app developers' lawsuit for $353 million

articles.summary: The Indian government has introduced a fortnightly quota system for sugar mills to improve supply. Under this rule, mills must sell at least 40% of their allocation in the first week and the rest in the following week. The government stated that previously, sugar sold early in the month was often lifted late, creating artificial scarcity. This policy aims to ensure timely distribution and availability of sugar.
articles.raw_summary: Under the fortnightly quota, sugar mills will be required to sell at least 40% of the allocation in the first week and the remaining quantity in the succeeding week. It was observed that in certain cases, sugar sold by mills at the beginning of the month was being dispatched or lifted by buyers only towards the end of the month, leading to artificial scarcity, the government said in a statement.

articles.title: Opinion: The problem with a threshold-based MDR
articles.summary: The article examines ongoing debates about UPI pricing in India, focusing on balancing system financing with promoting widespread adoption. It highlights that while consumer and person-to-person transactions remain fee-free, a proposed cap on merchant transactions aims to encourage payment splitting but may not generate sufficient revenue for the system. The discussion emphasizes the need to remove arbitrary thresholds to support economic growth in digital payments.
articles.raw_summary: The ongoing discussions around UPI pricing are shifting towards ensuring system financing while still promoting widespread adoption. Consumers will enjoy fee-free transactions, and person-to-person payments will continue to incur no charges. A new suggested cap on merchant transactions aims to boost payment splitting. However, this practice raises processing volumes yet fails to generate essential revenue for the system. It is crucial to remove arbitrary thresholds to facilitate economic growth.

articles.title: Meta child safety settlement explained: What changes for teens on Instagram and Facebook?
articles.summary: Meta has agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle a US legal case over the harmful impact of its platforms, Facebook and Instagram, on children. As part of the settlement, Meta will introduce new limits on teen usage of these platforms. The case highlights broader concerns about child safety and digital well-being, which are relevant to global discussions on platform regulation and data privacy.
articles.raw_summary: Meta will pay up to $18 billion to settle a US legal battle over its platforms' impact on children, agreeing to overhaul Facebook and Instagram with new teen usage limits.

articles.title: Mpox is back – and in new countries. How can this outbreak be contained?
articles.summary: A new outbreak of mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, has been reported in Guinea-Bissau, marking the country's first case. Since 2022, nearly 190,000 confirmed cases have been reported across 145 countries, with children particularly affected in recent outbreaks. The virus, which had previously seen smaller, localized outbreaks in Africa, is now spreading more widely. Public health experts are examining what has changed to drive this resurgence.

articles.summary: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto has launched a 24-district campaign across Jharkhand, demanding reforms in how recruitment exams are conducted in the state. Mahto, who is leading the initiative, is advocating for changes in recruitment policies that could impact job opportunities for students.
